snapshots.name: Faust
snapshots.body: An aging scholar, master of every field of learning available to him, yet consumed by despair at how little any of it has actually taught him. His restless dissatisfaction opens the play and sets its wager with the devil in motion.

snapshots.name: Mephistopheles
snapshots.body: A devil who strikes a wager with the Lord that he can lead Faust astray, then appears to Faust himself in the form of a traveling scholar. He offers Faust a pact: his service in this life for Faust's soul in the next.

snapshots.name: Margaret
snapshots.body: A young, devout townswoman, also called Gretchen, whom Faust becomes determined to seduce with Mephistopheles's help. Her simple household and pious habits are established well before Faust ever approaches her.

snapshots.name: Wagner
snapshots.body: Faust's earnest, bookish famulus, who admires his master's learning without sharing any of his restlessness or doubt. He interrupts Faust's private turmoil with talk of scholarship and rhetoric.

snapshots.name: the Lord
snapshots.body: God, who appears in the play's Prologue in Heaven presiding over a council of archangels. He accepts Mephistopheles's wager to tempt Faust, confident that a good man, even erring, keeps some sense of the right way.

snapshots.name: RAPHAEL
snapshots.body: An archangel who speaks in the Prologue in Heaven, praising the harmony of the created universe. His hymn opens the celestial council at which Mephistopheles proposes his wager.

snapshots.name: GABRIEL
snapshots.body: An archangel who speaks alongside Raphael and Michael in the Prologue in Heaven. His part of the hymn dwells on the turning of the earth and the alternation of day and night.

snapshots.name: MICHAEL
snapshots.body: An archangel who completes the trio praising creation in the Prologue in Heaven. His contribution to the hymn concerns storms and the violence of nature within an order that still holds together.

snapshots.name: Valentine
snapshots.body: Margaret's brother, a soldier proud of his sister's reputation and quick to defend her honor. He returns from service to find rumors about her circulating in the town.

snapshots.name: Martha
snapshots.body: Margaret's neighbor, a widow whose own household troubles make her a willing and rather worldly confidante. Mephistopheles uses her house as a convenient cover for arranging Faust's meetings with Margaret.

snapshots.name: Frosch
snapshots.body: One of a group of young men drinking and carousing in Auerbach's Cellar in Leipzig, the tavern scene where Faust and Mephistopheles make their first public stop. He is the loudest of the group in calling for songs and wine.

snapshots.name: Brander
snapshots.body: One of the drinking companions in Auerbach's Cellar, who offers a mocking song of his own when the mood turns rowdy. He and his fellow revelers become the target of one of Mephistopheles's tricks.

snapshots.name: Siebel
snapshots.body: Another of the young men drinking in Auerbach's Cellar, quick to join in the group's boasting and drinking songs. He is among those caught off guard by Mephistopheles's magic in the tavern scene.

snapshots.name: Altmayer
snapshots.body: The fourth of the carousing companions in Auerbach's Cellar, part of the rowdy company Faust and Mephistopheles encounter on their first outing together. He shares in the group's drinking and their eventual confusion.

snapshots.name: Witch
snapshots.body: An old sorceress who keeps the kitchen where Mephistopheles brings Faust to be magically restored to youth. Her potion and her strange household of animal familiars mark one of the play's more grotesque comic scenes.

snapshots.name: Student
snapshots.body: A young man newly arrived to begin his university studies, who comes seeking Faust's guidance and instead finds Mephistopheles impersonating him. He receives a satirical tour of the university's various faculties.
